Content:
We know that multiplication and division are opposite operations. So, to divide a number by ten, we remove a zero from the end of the number. For example,

Content:
[MATH: \require{cancel}
520 \div 10 = 52\!\cancel{0} = 52.]

items.readable_text:
Content:
We can use a similar method to divide whole numbers by [MATH: 100] and [MATH: 1,000.]

Content:
To divide a number by one hundred, we remove two zeros from the end of the number. For example,

Content:
[MATH: \require{cancel}
6,500 \div 100 = 6,5\!\cancel{00} = 65.]

Content:
This method only works for whole numbers that end in at least two zeros.

Content:
Similarly, to divide a whole number by one thousand, we remove three zeros from the end of the number. For example,

Content:
[MATH: \require{cancel}
32,000 \div 1,000 = 32,\!\!\cancel{000} = 32.]

Content:
This method only works for whole numbers that end in at least three zeros.

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Item 8 — Tutorial: Dividing Whole Numbers by One Hundred and One Thousand

Content:
We can use a similar method to divide whole numbers by [MATH: 100] and [MATH: 1,000.]

Content:
To divide a number by one hundred, we remove two zeros from the end of the number. For example,

Content:
[MATH: \require{cancel}
6,500 \div 100 = 6,5\!\cancel{00} = 65.]

Content:
This method only works for whole numbers that end in at least two zeros.

Content:
Similarly, to divide a whole number by one thousand, we remove three zeros from the end of the number. For example,

Content:
[MATH: \require{cancel}
32,000 \div 1,000 = 32,\!\!\cancel{000} = 32.]

Content:
This method only works for whole numbers that end in at least three zeros.

[MATH: 28, 000 ÷ 100|=; 28, 000|=; 280]

Therefore, [MATH: 280] liters of water was lost every minute.
